body: Cities around the world are building more bike lanes, hoping to cut traffic and air pollution at the same time.
全球不少城市正在增建自行车道，希望同时减少交通拥堵和空气污染。
Cycling is not only good for the planet; doctors say it also lowers stress and keeps the heart healthy with very low risk of injury.
骑车不仅对环境好，医生还指出它能减压、护心，而且受伤风险很低。
Still, many people hesitate because of unsafe roads or no place to shower at work — small problems that better city planning could fix.
但许多人仍犹豫，原因多是道路不安全、或单位没地方冲澡——这些小问题，靠更好的城市规划就能解决。

articles.zh: 那些让人不舒服的邮件
body: We all get blunt or careless emails, and they can ruin a working relationship before a project even starts.
我们都收到过生硬或马虎的邮件，它们甚至能在项目开始前就毁掉一段工作关系。
Experts suggest pausing before you send: read it as if you were the receiver, and soften words like 'you must' or 'wrong'.
专家建议发出前先停一下：把自己当收件人读一遍，把'你必须''你错了'这类词放缓和。
A short polite line at the end, such as 'thanks for your patience', can turn a cold message into a friendly one.
结尾加一句简短的客套，比如'感谢你的耐心'，就能把冷冰冰的信息变亲切。
Family dinners often feel stressful because everyone is tired and phones keep buzzing at the table.
家庭聚餐常让人紧张，因为大家都累，手机还不停在桌上响。
Cooks say the trick is to lower the bar: simple food, no screens, and let everyone help a little with setting the table.
做饭的人说窍门是降低标准：简单饭菜、不碰屏幕、让每人都帮点小忙摆桌。
When the mood is calm, children actually eat better and talk more — which is the real point of eating together.
气氛一放松，孩子反而吃得更好、话也更多——这才是一起吃饭的真正意义。
tips: 降低标准 / 放低要求

body: Many parents worry that tablets and phones steal too much of their children's day.
许多家长担心平板和手机占掉了孩子太多时间。
Instead of strict bans, child experts suggest 'joint screen time' — watching or playing together, then talking about it.
儿童专家不建议硬性禁止，而是建议'一起看屏幕'——陪着一起看、一起玩，然后聊一聊。
Clear rules, like no phones at meals and a fixed bedtime, work better than angry arguments every night.
清晰的规矩，比如吃饭不碰手机、固定睡觉时间，比每晚吵架管用得多。

articles.en: How Advertisers Make Us Spend Money
articles.zh: 商家是怎么让我们掏钱的
body: Shops use colour, music and layout to guide where your eyes go and what your hand reaches for.
商店用颜色、音乐和陈列，引导你的眼睛看哪、手伸向哪。
'Scarcity' tricks like 'only 3 left' or 'sale ends tonight' push us to buy now instead of thinking it over.
'稀缺'套路，比如'只剩3件''今晚结束'，逼我们立刻买，而不是先想想。
Knowing these tricks helps you pause and ask: do I really need this, or am I just being nudged?
识破这些套路，你就能停一下自问：我是真需要，还是只是被推了一把？
